# Full results

Run finished 2026-11-24. 5 rounds, provider order shuffled each round (seed 20261124).
Every container was limited to 4 CPUs and 4 GB. Host: Apple M4 Max, 16 cores, 64 GB, Docker 29.7.2 (linux/arm64).
Client: Playwright 1.65.1 on Node v22.18.0, connecting with `connectOverCDP`.

Times are medians in milliseconds. Square brackets are the 95% bootstrap confidence interval of the median. Bold marks the best value in a row.

## What was tested

| Browser | Engine | Reports itself as | Image | Image size | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Headless Chromium (baseline) | Chromium headless-shell, no wrapper | 159.0.8154.13 | `chromedp/headless-shell:latest`<br>`sha256:381353d3530a` | 147 MB | BSD-3-Clause |
| Browserless | Chromium behind the Browserless router | 159.0.8154.6 | `ghcr.io/browserless/chromium:latest`<br>`sha256:62a1025c4f92` | 1,012 MB | SSPL-1.0 or commercial |
| Steel Browser | Chromium behind the Steel session API | 156.0.8078.108 | `ghcr.io/steel-dev/steel-browser:latest`<br>`sha256:c68ff8d92912` | 967 MB | Apache-2.0 |
| Obscura | Own Rust engine with V8 (not Chromium) | 145.0.0.0 | `h4ckf0r0day/obscura:latest`<br>`sha256:e70c2abc925f` | 97 MB | Apache-2.0 |

What "opening a session" means for each:

- **Headless Chromium (baseline):** Connects to an already-running browser process and uses its default context.
- **Browserless:** Each WebSocket connection launches a new Chromium process, which is killed on disconnect.
- **Steel Browser:** POST /v1/sessions relaunches Chromium with a clean profile; the client then connects over CDP. One session at a time.
- **Obscura:** Each CDP connection gets its own thread and V8 isolates inside one long-lived server process.
